records.scope: Season-one final four released guide entries: 81 selected profiles, named official narrative/trivia/biography evidence and direct/remote distinctions. Original-US date policy retained. No release, edition, credit or episode-inventory changes.
limitations: All fourteen season-one guide entries (fifteen numbered parts) now have selected-profile reviews, with 217 first-season connections. The final four use 81 considered profiles and named official narrative/trivia/biography evidence. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent. The other 52 guide entries await selected-profile review.

Trayvis’s vision, broadcast and physical meeting share one direct row with context. Alton/Trayvis interviews, Fulcrum’s remote conversation and Bail’s holographic greeting are transmissions. Ahsoka’s finale reveal and Vader’s Lothal arrival are direct scenes; later Kallus-Fulcrum biography is not assigned to the season-one contact.

The Sovereign, communications light-cruiser family, stolen rescue transport, Broken Horn and two distinct stolen/borrowed TIEs retain separate identities and scope. Mustafar is only a planned destination in Rebel Resolve but a system setting in the finale. No Gideon/Trask hull, generic Lambda, A-wing or technical metadata inferred.

Path of the Jedi distinguishes nightmare visions from direct scenes and Yoda’s remote communication through the Force. Mixed direct/vision contexts use one direct row with explanation; no real crew deaths or physical Yoda temple visit are asserted.

Fort Anaxes is the Rebels-era asteroid base. The displayed parade TIE and Inquisitor’s pursuit fighter are distinct. The Relentless has no assumed subclass and the landing shuttle has no assumed Lambda/Theta identity. No legacy technical fields inherited.

The combined Spark of Rebellion guide remains one review for parts 1–2. The later ABC Vader opening is excluded from original-pilot connections and remains a distinct documented version. No scene is assigned to an individual pilot part without evidence.

Obi-Wan’s holocron message, Trayvis’s broadcast and Luminara’s projected bait are transmissions. Luminara’s remains are also shown. Remote contacts followed by physical scenes use a single direct row with context; mentions, aliases and repeated names are not extra characters.
Episode inventory and writing credits do not establish every language mix, supplied master or frame-level version. Public references are not open media licences.

Normalized count: 75 numbered parts across four seasons (15/22/22/16), grouped into 66 official guide entries (14/20/19/13). This is an archive counting convention, not a universal count of playable streaming items. The four introductory shorts and the ABC revised pilot are excluded. Individual credits and appearances within combined parts are not inferred.

Current release-date research is restricted to the original US launch of each work and, when necessary to distinguish a documented version, its first US release. Existing sourced events are retained. Worldwide/Finland dates, later platform availability, routine rereleases and exhaustive master comparisons are deferred rather than factually resolved.

notes: Trayvis appears in Ezra’s vision, in a broadcast, and physically at the meeting. The combined row is direct with all three contexts explained. The vision is not a separate character or proof that Ezra correctly understood its meaning.

The six crew members have named actual scenes; the Ghost is the actual ending location. Zare and Kallus are supported by the narrative captions. The Inquisitor’s stated desire and the guide’s Related entry for Tua do not independently establish a direct scene in this selected text review.

The Senate building is a place on Lothal, not Coruscant’s Senate or a new planet. Trayvis’s protocol droids are not identified as C-3PO. Statements about Ezra’s parents do not create named physical parent appearances or independently establish their fate.

episodeReviews.scope: One released guide entry reviewed against 81 selected profiles using named official narrative, trivia and scoped biography evidence. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent; direct scenes and transmissions are distinguished, with mixed contexts explained.
notes: Fulcrum’s conversation with Hera is a remote transmission. The season-one identity is Ahsoka, explicitly revealed in the next guide’s caption 25; no second Fulcrum character or physical visit is created. Kallus later uses the same code name, but that later biography does not substitute him for this contact.

The stolen courier is distinct from Chopper impersonating it. Type/role profiles do not assert that every courier, probe or interrogation machine across works is the same individual, or that the episode establishes an exact droid serial/model number.

The Imperial light cruiser carrying communication logs is distinct from the Sovereign holding Kanan. Neither is identified with Gideon’s later ship, the Relentless or every generic Star Destroyer. The Broken Horn vessel is explicitly seen per trivia, not merely inferred from Vizago’s organization name.

Mustafar is the destination identified at the end, not yet an established current setting in this selected review. Kanan’s current detention aboard the Sovereign is explicitly identified, so its prison interior is included without claiming a Mustafar surface scene. Prisoner lists and mentions do not create Wookiee, parent or other character appearances.

episodeReviews.scope: One released guide entry reviewed against 81 selected profiles using named official narrative, trivia and scoped biography evidence. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent; direct scenes and transmissions are distinguished, with mixed contexts explained.
notes: Bail greets the crew by holographic transmission. Ahsoka is physically revealed as Fulcrum. The contact and code name are not an additional character, and the hologram does not identify Bail’s current planet.

Tarkin, Kallus and Vader are directly involved in the final Lothal scene: the ending caption is deliberately unnamed, so Kallus’s official biography caption 10 supplies the named identification. This is not the ABC-added pilot opening, a hologram or a later season-two Vader encounter.

The stolen TIE is explicitly the Fighter Flight craft, now repainted. The Inquisitor’s fighter is a different ship used by Kanan and Ezra. Repaint plans and cut earlier background scenes are not backfilled into old episodes; neither fighter is Vader’s TIE Advanced x1.

The stolen Imperial freighter is given a descriptive editorial scene label only, without assigning a Gozanti model or equating it to the later Trask freighter. The rescue target continues the Sovereign detention identified in Rebel Resolve; surrounding destroyers are not all that same ship.

Mustafar is now an established system setting for the rescue, not a claim that the rebels land on its surface. Kanan’s Master is recalled in dialogue, not established as an onscreen flashback. Ezra’s fall is followed by survival, not an actual death. The A-wing-inspired markings and engine-room design references do not create A-wing, Clone Wars cruiser or Macross appearances. The blockade runners’ exact hull identities remain open.
